title: Midday Recap, Nov. 13: Tech Leads Stocks Lower as Nvidia Extends Its Slide
dek: The Nasdaq was down about 1.6% and the S&P 500 about 1.1% by late morning, with chipmakers leading the decline while the Dow was near flat and the 10-year yield held above 5%.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Traders on the floor of a stock exchange

keyPoints: At 11:59 a.m. ET the Nasdaq Composite was recently down about 1.6%, the S&P 500 about 1.1% and the Dow about 0.4% (Investopedia live coverage).

body:
US stocks were lower late Friday morning, and technology did most of the damage. By 11:59 a.m. ET, the Nasdaq Composite was recently down about 1.6% and the S&P 500 about 1.1%, according to Investopedia's live coverage. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down about 0.4%, close to flat by comparison. Thursday's closes were 25,366.09 for the Nasdaq and 7,592.40 for the S&P 500 (AP).

## How the open played out

Stocks opened higher, then gave up their gains within the first half hour. At 10:06 a.m. ET, CNBC's live page had the Nasdaq down 0.9% and the S&P 500 down 0.6%, with the Dow near flat (StockTitan, summarizing CNBC). The slide widened from there.

Chipmakers were the weakest group. AMD fell about 11% and led the S&P 500 decliners. Broadcom, Intel, Marvell and Micron each fell more than 5%. Applied Materials dropped about 6% even though its quarterly results beat expectations, and the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) was down nearly 6%.

## Nvidia and the movers

Nvidia was down about 4% at midday, after a drop of more than 4% on Thursday when Jensen Huang stepped down as chief executive. StockTitan's real-time data put the shares about 14% below their Nov. 6 close at 11 a.m. ET. Colette Kress is serving as interim chief executive.

Microsoft was unchanged after the company said it was making progress on an outage that disrupted Outlook and Teams. It had been down more than 1% before the open. Cerebras had jumped about 16% premarket after reporting a surprise profit and revenue above forecasts, and it was still up 11.6% at 8:04 a.m. ET. Cisco fell about 6% despite strong results and an upbeat outlook. Apple rose about 1% to a fresh all-time high, while Tesla and Alphabet each fell about 2%.

Among smaller names, Modine rose more than 26% after Bloomberg reported that Samsung was in takeover talks with it, and Newsmax gained about 29% after its third-quarter results (StockTitan).

## Rates, oil and crypto

The 10-year Treasury yield was about 5.14% at 11:59 a.m. ET (Investopedia). Earlier, Yahoo Finance had it at 5.16%, its highest level since October. WTI crude was little changed near $88.65 a barrel.

Bitcoin traded around $68,600, below $70,000 for the first time since August, and Strategy (MSTR) was down nearly 5% (Investopedia).

## What to watch

The October producer price index came in slightly below forecasts, but its 6.5% annual rate kept a December rate hike firmly priced. Yahoo Finance reports that Nvidia's fiscal third-quarter earnings come next Tuesday, Nov. 17, which makes the chip group's leadership the main question for the afternoon session. The open shows the market is debating whether the AI trade is losing leadership or only pausing after the Huang exit.

marketImpact.summary: Tech is carrying the midday decline. The pressure comes from chip-sector selling tied to Nvidia's leadership vacuum, a 10-year yield above 5% and weaker crypto, while the Dow's near-flat move suggests the damage is concentrated in AI-linked names rather than the whole market.
marketImpact.timeframe: Rest of Friday, Nov. 13, then Nvidia earnings next Tuesday
